thread: Valuation Office Survey 1910 — location request (OS Glamorgan XLVII.6, Llandough)
subject: FOI — location only — Valuation Office Survey 1910, OS Glamorgan XLVII.6, Llandough / Great House Farm
body:
Freedom of Information Team,

This is a request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000. It is a location request only. I am not asking for a copy of the plan, a screen-room appointment, or production of the item until the location and physical-check status are confirmed.

Context. Glamorgan Archives, in reply 2026/4097b of 30 September 2026, identified Ordnance Survey sheet Glamorgan XLVII.6 as the sheet relevant to Great House Farm / Ty Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, and directed me to the Valuation Office Survey 1910-1915 maps held by The National Archives.

Please state, for the Valuation Office field book, plan, and index covering that sheet for the parish of Llandough (Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Glamorgan):

1. The series, piece, and item references (including any IR 58, IR 121, IR 124, IR 125, IR 126, IR 127, IR 128 or successor reference that applies).
2. The accession, box, shelf, or other store location used by your staff.
3. The Discovery catalogue identifier.
4. Whether a member of staff has physically checked that the item is in that location: yes, no, or not answered. If yes, who checked it and on what date, and which store.
5. Whether the item is open, closed, or retained by another department, and if closed the series and the FOI route for a closed record.
6. The systems searched, and whether a physical file or plan was retrieved rather than a catalogue-only search.

I am not asking you to interpret ownership or to comment on any legal proceedings. Please treat a “not held” answer as incomplete unless you name the systems searched and whether a physical item was retrieved.

Please quote this email as the request and give the statutory deadline.

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread: Valuation Office Survey 1910 — location request (OS Glamorgan XLVII.6, Llandough)
from: FOI Manager, Freedom of Information Centre, The National Archives (FOIRequests@nationalarchives.gov.uk)
subject: RE: FOI — location only — Valuation Office Survey 1910, OS Glamorgan XLVII.6, Llandough / Great House Farm
body:
Dear Sion Buckler,

Thank you for your email.

Based on the information you have provided, we believe that this is the Valuation Office map covering the property you have referred to: https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/details/r/C1667398 (IR 131/4/96).

Unfortunately, there is no way of identifying the relevant IR field book on our catalogue without additional information. We would need the income tax parish and the assessment number, which we would expect to be found via the map linked above (IR 131/4/96). We have checked the Genealogist website which has digitised some of these records, but its coverage appears not to include Glamorgan.

We have made a guess that the income tax parish is Penarth, but we would still need the assessment number of the individual farm in order to identify the right field book: https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/results/r/1?_q=penarth&_cr=IR%2058&_dss=range&_ro=any&_srt=1)

Your options for accessing information from IR 131/4/96 is to either travel to Kew to review it and ascertain the field book number yourself, or to request a paid search by TNA staff, or hire an independent researcher.

Details on the options available for paid research can be found via the following pages:

https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/help-with-your-research/paying-for-research/

A public authority is allowed to charge fees for access to information under section 9 of the FOI Act. The prices we charge are set out by the Fees Regulations under the Public Records Act (1958), and are based on recovering the costs of providing the services. Fees are typically charged for research and provision of information within open records in TNA's collection.

Information on booking a visit to The National Archives and how to register for a reader's ticket can be found here: https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/visit/researching-here/booking-a-visit-to-view-documents/

If you are able to identify the relevant records from our catalogue to which your enquiry below relates, you are welcome to request information regarding their production history or any other recorded metadata held in relation to them. Please submit a new request to FOIRequests@nationalarchives.gov.uk

We hope this advice is of assistance in your research.

Yours sincerely,

FOI Manager
Freedom of Information Centre
The National Archives

thread: CAS-347296-M0V4Y1 — FOI on records of Great House Farm and BP v Buckler (incl. internal review CAS-356384)
subject: Internal review — CAS-347296-M0V4Y1 / CRM:007302479 — Great House Farm / Tÿ Mawr, Llandough
body:
Quality Manager
The National Archives
complaints@nationalarchives.gov.uk
cc: FOIRequests@nationalarchives.gov.uk

Sirs/Madam,

Internal review of CAS-347296-M0V4Y1 / CRM:007302479, disclosure dated 23 September 2026.
Requester: Sion Buckler.

I am not asking TNA to decide title. I am asking whether the disclosure answered the request.

The request asked whether records relating to Great House Farm / Tÿ Mawr and to BP Properties Ltd v Buckler exist in your systems, where they came from, and whether they were transferred, retained, destroyed or disposed of. A finding that TNA does not itself hold a court file is not a finding that no transfer, accession or destruction entry exists.

Please determine, on review:

1. Which catalogues, transfer lists and destruction registers were searched.
2. Whether any WELSH OFFICE, court-administration, HO or DEFE series was considered and excluded, and why.
3. Whether the destroyed European Commission file in Buckler v United Kingdom, Application 14464/88 (file destroyed in 2000; decision of 14 April 1989 remains on HUDOC), has any TNA counterpart or transfer note.
4. What, if anything, is held about the existence or disposal of those records, as distinct from the records themselves.

The public evidence index is https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/ . The 1987 Court of Appeal decided possession, limitation and the October 1974 letters. It did not decide the documentary root of the farmhouse parcel. Transfer and destruction entries go to that separate question. They are evidential questions, not findings against TNA.

Please preserve anything in scope while the review is open. Nothing in this letter abandons any claim. This is not a claim form.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread: CAS-347296-M0V4Y1 — FOI on records of Great House Farm and BP v Buckler (incl. internal review CAS-356384)
subject: RE: Freedom of Information Request: Reference CAS-347296-M0V4Y1 — clarification
body:
FOI Centre,

Reference CAS-347296-M0V4Y1

Thank you for your email of 20 August asking me to clarify scope. I apologise for the delay in replying. Please take the request off hold on the following basis.

1. The FOI request (CAS-347296) is limited to the six numbered questions in my email of 13 August: whether the searches were limited to the PRO and RW series and four place-name terms; whether the named companies, court proceedings and application references were searched; whether TNA holds any transfer, accession, retention, destruction or disposal information for records concerning the property, companies or litigation; the reason for any "not held" answer; whether HMC9/311 was checked; and whether there are central-government, court or departmental records on the litigation or entities that would not be found by a place-name search.

2. My email of 20 August about the National Farm Survey and the Glamorgan War Agricultural Executive Committee (1936–1950) is not part of this FOI request. Please treat it as a records enquiry under the existing case CAS-344046-K1S1R2. My chase of that case on 20 August bounced from foi@nationalarchives.gov.uk, so I would be grateful if you could pass it to the Records Enquiries team.

I am not asking TNA to research the contents of uncatalogued records, only to tell me what recorded information it holds about the searches, the catalogue and the transfer or disposal of relevant records.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber and Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

Dear Ret'd Sergeant Sion Buckler,

Thank you for your email, dated 30th September.

To clarify, you provided The National Archives with clarification to your FOI request on the 2nd September 2026 and we provided a final response on 23rd September 2026.

Also on 23rd September 2026, you requested an internal review into the handling of your FOI request. This case reference for this internal review is CAS-356384.

For ease of reference, please find attached the final response to your original request which contains details of your original request and the clarification you provided.

Please note, the request with case reference CAS-344046 relates to your original enquiry to The National Archives. We decided to handle this as an FOI request, with the new case reference CAS-347296.

Yours sincerely,
